images.after: What the FTC requires, and what is only good practice
images.title: What a disclosure has to do
images.alt: Four cards: disclose material connections, match the format, make it unavoidable online, and use words people understand.
images.caption: The FTC's test is whether someone reading that recommendation will see and understand the disclosure.

items.title: Disclose the connection
items.text: Commissions, free products, payment and discount codes that earn you something

items.title: Match the format
items.text: Written needs written, spoken needs spoken, a video that does both needs both

items.title: Make it unavoidable
items.text: No clicking, scrolling to a footer or opening another page to find it

items.title: Use plain words
items.text: "Affiliate link" alone may not be enough; say that you get paid

images.after: Where the disclosure goes on each platform
images.title: Where the disclosure goes
images.alt: Table of where to place an affiliate disclosure on blog posts, video, social captions and email, and what not to rely on for each.
images.caption: On every platform, the disclosure sits with the recommendation, not somewhere the reader has to go looking.

rows: Top of the post, before any link
A link labelled disclosure or legal

A description note on its own
At the start of the caption
